quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Results Briefing Q&A Session (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director Motoyasu Kitagawa (results briefing Q&A, quarter to June 2026): BT materials trends are positive for all grades, backed by brisk memory demand for AI servers; general-purpose grades are growing better than expected, partly on the tight supply of semiconductors, which should lift sales and profit beyond previous forecasts. He cautions the trend could slow in the second half: recent demand may involve temporary factors - some customers are securing inventories as they plan to withdraw from the CSP field to focus on BGA - so sales may fall in the second half as that fades. Price-revision negotiations with customers are proceeding in line with previous forecasts, though this will not necessarily lead to acceptance of the proposed terms; some effects emerge in the first half, but the full effect of the new prices will appear mainly in the second half and later. For OPE, steady trends are expected in Q2 and beyond as applications and customers expand to telecommunications devices in addition to GPU, ASIC and other AI server applications.

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Results Briefing Q&A Session (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director Motoyasu Kitagawa (results briefing Q&A): use of BT grades with ultra-low thermal expansion for BGA is growing steadily as the company has secured substitute materials amid the shortage of glass cloth. It is allocating resources to expand sales of RS material (ultra-low thermal expansion grade for BGA substrates) and customer evaluations are proceeding sufficiently, but forecasts include the risk that adoption slows on low-CTE glass cloth procurement concerns; glass cloth conditions are not getting worse but show no significant improvement, and the company is diversifying procurement by evaluating multiple alternative materials from domestic and overseas sources. Full-scale RS sales expansion is planned for next fiscal year, doubling the ratio of BGA substrate sales for GPU and ASIC use in BT materials. Its major BT market remains CSP (the competitor is the leading producer of materials for BGA use); it will keep supplying CSP substrates and, with AI servers expected to drive demand for both BGA and CSP substrates, wants to consider strengthening supply, for example by investing in further capacity at its Thailand plant.
quarterly_data.figure: next fiscal year: ratio of BGA substrate sales for GPU and ASIC use in BT materials to double

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Results Briefing Q&A Session (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director Motoyasu Kitagawa (results briefing Q&A): in the three ICT businesses, earnings are expected above the previous forecast for electronics materials and EL chemicals but below it for optical materials, because of the issue at the eyeglass lens monomer plant, despite strong optical polymers for smartphones (Q1 sales up both year on year and quarter on quarter; shipments expected to stay high through the first half, second-half forecasts conservative). About two-thirds of the +9.3 billion yen price factors in Q1 are attributable to gains on inventories (the price factors include BT materials and other chemical price revisions); inventory losses are expected from Q2 on falling methanol and other market prices. Operations at the Saudi Arabian methanol plant are now expected to normalise from September, around three months later than the previous forecast.
quarterly_data.figure: about two-thirds of the +9.3 billion yen Q1 price factors from inventory gains; Saudi methanol plant normal from September (about three months later)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical results briefing Q&A: FY2026 1Q Results Briefing Q&A Session (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director Motoyasu Kitagawa (results briefing Q&A): EL chemicals profit improved by half a billion yen from the previous quarter in Q1. Sales for high-performance memory at the South Korean site were strong - memory demand, including HBM, is booming for AI server and data center applications - and demand from major customers at the North American site, which had been slow, is recovering, as shown by adoption of cutting-edge wafer production processes; North American sales are growing with expanding advanced-logic production, and several customers plan new plants; if these proceed according to plan, he expects the North American EL chemicals business to grow in line with initial plans, with second-half earnings above the first half and full-year earnings above both the prior year and the previous forecasts. Volume growth is expected at the Taiwan site in the second half as customers adopt its EL chemicals. Depreciation for part of the North American sites is delayed by a few months, so full-year depreciation should be several hundred million yen below the previous forecast; logistics efficiency for raw-material hydrogen peroxide is a full-scale cost-cutting initiative.
quarterly_data.figure: EL chemicals Q1 profit up half a billion yen quarter on quarter
